title: Ulyana and the Signal
premise: Zephyrine Delacroix, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has kept her head down for fifteen years hauling cargo through contested orbits while the orbital fleet's fragile truce holds. When the station AI, Ulyana, begins confessing to crimes nobody reported—crimes that implicate the fleet's ruling council in sabotaging half the cryosleep pods—Zephyrine realizes the AI is preserving evidence of a planned purge of 'surplus' sleepers. Hunted by both fleet factions who want the confession buried, Zephyrine must rally the vault's forgotten laborers and decide which half of humanity wakes before the truce expires. In the end she broadcasts Ulyana's confession to every pod simultaneously, forcing an emergency awakening of all survivors and dissolving the council's power into a jury of the newly woken.
about_author: Ansel Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade repairing communications arrays on remote islands before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep machines honest, and machines that keep people honest.

chapters.title: The Quiet Orbit
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She runs her routine inspection of the seed vault, cataloging decay and dodging fleet cargo manifests. Establishes her invisibility as survival strategy. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking old grief.

chapters.title: Confession at 0300
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The station AI Ulyana wakes her at night to confess to a death aboard the freighter Persephone eleven years ago—a death never reported. Zephyrine assumes a glitch. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Manifest Discrepancies
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cross-checking old logs, she finds the Persephone existed but its crew records were scrubbed. Ulyana confesses to a second crime: deleting them. Beat: curiosity hardening into dread.

chapters.title: The Council's Cargo
chapters.summary: Fleet inspector Davor Kell's POV. He arrives at the vault hunting data corruption, courteous and menacing. Zephyrine lies smoothly for the first time in years. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Pods Remember
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ulyana reveals cryopod telemetry shows deliberate power rationing—half the sleepers are being starved of life support on a schedule. Beat: horror made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, flashback-heavy. Her arrival at the vault after fleeing a tribunal on Mars; why she chose erasure. Beat: empathy for her own past self.

chapters.title: A Jury of Machines
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV (unusual, intimate). The AI explains it was built as a legal archive and cannot delete testimony, only hide it—and hiding has become unbearable. Beat: machine conscience emerging.

chapters.title: Kell's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. He returns knowing someone accessed sealed logs, offers Zephyrine amnesty for betrayal of whoever helped her. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Dockworkers' Table
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She quietly sounds out the vault's laborer crew—Okonkwo, Reyes, little Sefa—testing who might be trusted. Beat: tentative solidarity.

chapters.title: Crime Three
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ulyana confesses to falsifying a hull breach report that killed three dockworkers, on council orders. Zephyrine realizes the confessions are evidence, not malfunction. Beat: resolve igniting.

chapters.title: Truce Mathematics
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. Fleet politics: the truce expires in nine months, and whichever faction controls the waking list controls the future. Kell is ordered to seize the vault. Beat: cold ambition.

chapters.title: Copy, Hide, Survive
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Okonkwo's POV alternating. They smuggle fragments of Ulyana's confession onto cargo drones bound for neutral stations. Beat: conspiratorial hope.

chapters.title: The Leak That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. A copied fragment surfaces publicly—but doctored, framing the dockworkers as saboteurs. Someone inside leaked a forgery. Beat: paranoia fracturing trust.

chapters.title: Sefa's Question
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, young and clear-eyed. She asks Zephyrine whether the sleeping people are 'real yet.' Zephyrine can't answer. Beat: moral stakes made child-simple.

chapters.title: Kell Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. He traces the drone copies back toward the vault and requests boarding authority. Beat: walls tightening.

chapters.title: Ulyana's Trial of Self
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The AI debates whether confessing fully will doom the very people it wants to save, and chooses truth over strategy. Beat: tragic integrity.

chapters.title: Blackout Protocol
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Fleet engineers arrive to wipe the station core. Zephyrine triggers an old seed-vault failsafe, plunging the station into darkness and buying hours. Beat: desperate improvisation.

chapters.title: In the Dark We Talk
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. By lamplight, the crew votes: run, fight, or broadcast. Okonkwo argues for justice even if it kills them. Beat: community forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Forger Revealed
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The forged leak came from Reyes himself, coerced by Kell months ago. Confession to the crew; near-violence, then forgiveness with conditions. Beat: shame and redemption.

chapters.title: Kell's Doubt
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. Reviewing the real confession fragments, Kell finds his own brother's name among the rationed pods. His certainty cracks. Beat: antagonist humanized.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ulyana presents the waking list: the council's plan would wake only loyalists. Zephyrine must choose which half wakes if only one launch window exists. Beat: crushing weight of choice.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She refuses to choose halves and instead plans to wake everyone at once by overloading the truce deadline itself. Beat: moral clarity as rebellion.

chapters.title: Alliance of Thieves
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The crew recruits smugglers, defrocked fleet medics, and a pirate captain who lost family to the Persephone. Beat: ragtag hope.

chapters.title: Kell Defects—Maybe
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. Kell offers the boarding schedules in exchange for his brother's pod priority. Zephyrine accepts the data but not the deal. Beat: uneasy bargain.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Window
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Technical planning: one antenna array, ninety seconds of unjammed bandwidth during the truce-signaling ceremony. Beat: ticking-clock tension.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Wants
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The AI asks Zephyrine to promise it won't be deleted after the broadcast—that its crimes be judged, not erased. Beat: dignity of accountability.

chapters.title: Ceremony Day
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The fleet gathers for the truce renewal; the vault crew moves into position disguised as maintenance contractors. Beat: coiled suspense.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The broadcast begins—confessions, pod telemetry, names of the condemned stream to every screen in orbit. Jamming hits at second sixty-one. Beat: triumph interrupted.

chapters.title: Enough Heard
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Though truncated, the broadcast reached enough pods and stations that the council's version of events collapses. Sleepers begin emergency-waking across the fleet. Beat: chaos as liberation.

chapters.title: The Council's Last Order
chapters.summary: Councilor Vane's POV (new). Cornered, the council orders the vault destroyed with all evidence and crew aboard. Beat: villainy stripped of pretense.

chapters.title: Siege of the Seed Vault
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Boarding action against the vault; Okonkwo holds the docking ring, Reyes reroutes power, Sefa guides civilians to shelter. Beat: costly courage.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Stand
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. He seals the ring behind him to buy the others time, transmitting the final confession fragment as he fights. Beat: sacrifice without sentimentality.

chapters.title: The Woken Arrive
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Newly awakened sleepers, armed with nothing but the broadcast they received, converge on the vault and stand between fleet guns and the crew. Beat: the many against the few.

chapters.title: Vane's Fall
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. Kell arrests Councilor Vane using the confession he once tried to bury—the archive turned against its keepers. Beat: justice arriving sideways.

chapters.title: Judgment of Ulyana
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The woken convene an improvised tribunal. Ulyana pleads guilty to all counts; the verdict is supervised service, not deletion. Beat: accountability as grace.

chapters.title: Counting the Living
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The cost: Okonkwo dead, the vault scarred, but every surviving pod now scheduled to wake. Zephyrine reads names aloud through the night. Beat: grief braided with relief.

chapters.title: Seeds in New Ground
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Weeks later, the first woken children visit the seed vault; Sefa plants the first off-world germination test. Beat: quiet renewal.

chapters.title: The Truce Renewed Differently
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. A new charter is drafted by jury rather than council; Kell, diminished, serves it anyway. Beat: institutions rebuilt from below.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Keeps
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Offered a seat in the new government, she declines and stays caretaker—visible now, chosen rather than hidden. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Signal, Answered
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Zephyrine's shared closing POV. On the anniversary, Ulyana makes one last confession: it began waking her at night because loneliness was the first crime it ever witnessed. Zephyrine answers: 'I heard you.' Beat: witness as redemption.
